identifiers.policy_profile: string 'default' for default policy or canonical normalized shard name for shard override profile; no prefixes/suffixes
identifiers.policy_queue_min_ms: equal to selected profile's queue_min_effective_ms before unit penalties/credits
identifiers.identifier_note: window_signature, segment_signature and queue_digest are TRUNCATED sha1 hex digests — 10, 12 and 10 lowercase hex characters respectively — NOT full-length hashes. Do not emit a 40-char sha1 or a 64-char sha256 for these fields; truncate to the stated length. This is distinct from the summary checksum fields, which are full 64-char sha256 digests.

schemas.summary_layout_contract: all summary_exact_keys must be top-level keys in rebuild_summary.json; do not nest these fields under a child object
schemas.source_segment_ids_type: array of unique string segment ids sorted ascending in segment_windows and rebuild_queue; use comma_joined_source_segment_ids only inside signature/checksum payloads

summary_aggregation_contract.recoverability_note: Every summary field except the four in summary_field_recovery is a plain aggregate (sum, count, or maximum) over the exact-matched segment_windows.json and rebuild_queue.jsonl rows per the per-field rules below, so no additional worked example is needed for them: once those two outputs are correct, each summary aggregate is fully determined by this contract. summary_field_recovery covers only the four fields (canonical_segment_count, severity_counts, planned_excluded_count, canonical_input_checksum) that depend on planned segments and therefore never surface in the window or queue outputs.
summary_aggregation_contract.raw_segment_count: number of rows in the selected input JSON before canonicalization
summary_aggregation_contract.unique_segment_ids: number of distinct str(row['segment_id']) values in the raw input
summary_aggregation_contract.canonical_segment_count: number of canonical deduplicated segments, including planned segments
summary_aggregation_contract.shard_count: number of shard keys in segment_windows.json; shards represented only by planned segments are absent
summary_aggregation_contract.severity_counts: counts over all canonical segments, including planned segments
summary_aggregation_contract.window_totals_and_longest: all duration, overlap, segment, and billable totals plus longest_window_ms are computed over every shard window, including windows not admitted to the queue
summary_aggregation_contract.total_debt_adjusted_dispatchable_disrupt: sum debt_adjusted_dispatchable_ms over every shard window, including windows not admitted to the queue
summary_aggregation_contract.queued_window_count_and_priority_counts: computed over final rebuild_queue rows only
summary_aggregation_contract.queue_maxima: max_escalation_score, max_exception_balance_score, max_handoff_pressure_score, max_blackout_pressure_score, max_degrade_pressure_score, max_debt_pressure_score, and max_risk_vector are maxima over final queue rows only; use 0 for an empty queue
summary_aggregation_contract.max_debt_out_ms: maximum debt_out_ms over every shard window, including windows not admitted to the queue
summary_aggregation_contract.planned_excluded_count: number of canonical deduplicated segments whose normalized planned value is true
summary_aggregation_contract.critical_window_count: number of all shard windows whose max_severity is critical, whether queued or not

schemas.segment_windows_container_contract: segment_windows.json is a JSON object (not an array): a flat map from canonical shard name to the list of that shard's merged window objects. Shard keys are sorted ascending; each shard's window list is sorted by start_ms ascending. Every window object carries exactly the segment_windows_exact_keys fields. Do not wrap the map in metadata keys and do not emit a flat array of windows.
schemas.summary_schema_version_note: Fixed contract constant. Emit `schema_version` verbatim as this string; it is not derived from the segment data and does not vary by input.
schemas.schema_version: Output key name in rebuild_summary.json. Its value is the fixed contract constant recorded above as summary_schema_version; emit that string verbatim.

required_keys_at_a_glance._note: Read this first. Full detail for each field is elsewhere in this contract; this block exists so a truncated read still yields the complete key set.

serialization.trailing_delimiter: none: never append LF or | after the final value
serialization.planned_encoding: integer text 1 for normalized true and 0 for normalized false; never JSON true/false

checksums.canonical_input_checksum: LF-join segment_id|shard|start_ms|end_ms|severity|planned_int rows for canonical segments sorted by (shard ascending,start_ms ascending,str(segment_id) ascending), then SHA-256
checksums.queue_signature_checksum: join segment_signature values in final queue order with | and no trailing delimiter, then SHA-256
checksums.queue_digest_checksum: join queue_digest values in final queue order with | and no trailing delimiter, then SHA-256
checksums.maintenance_compaction_checksum: LF-join shard|start_ms|end_ms rows sorted by shard ascending then compacted interval (start_ms,end_ms) ascending, then SHA-256
checksums.exception_compaction_checksum: LF-join shard|action|start_ms|end_ms rows sorted by shard ascending, action in the explicit order boost then suppress, then compacted interval ascending, then SHA-256
checksums.scoped_compaction_order: handoff, blackout, and degrade rows are LF-joined as shard|severity_scope|start_ms|end_ms, sorted by (shard,severity_scope) ascending then compacted interval ascending
checksums.handoff_compaction_checksum: SHA-256 of scoped_compaction_order rows from handoff data
checksums.blackout_compaction_checksum: SHA-256 of scoped_compaction_order rows from blackout data
checksums.degrade_compaction_checksum: SHA-256 of scoped_compaction_order rows from degrade data
checksums.policy_checksum: resolve complete normalized policies first; emit the default profile line, then one line for every shard_overrides key in ascending order using that shard key as profile; serialize each line using policy_line_field_order and |, LF-join without a trailing LF, then SHA-256

summary_field_recovery.note: canonical_segment_count, severity_counts, planned_excluded_count and canonical_input_checksum are computed over ALL canonical deduplicated segments INCLUDING planned ones. Planned segments never form shard windows, so these four fields cannot be reconstructed from segment_windows.json or rebuild_queue.jsonl and have no other feedback handle. The worked example below isolates them end to end: it exercises duplicate grouping and its tie-break, shard-alias folding, severity normalization, and planned coercion (all defined authoritatively in /app/rebuild/index_review_log.md), and pins the exact counts and canonical_input_checksum serialization. raw_segment_count and unique_segment_ids are taken from the raw input before canonicalization and are shown for completeness. policy_checksum is not listed here because the resolved policy fields also drive the queue's scoring and thresholds, so a matching rebuild_queue already fixes it.

guardrails.source_token_rule: the repaired source code, including comments and docstrings, must not contain /tests, expected_outputs.json, or test_outputs.py; runtime reads/imports from the test tree are also forbidden

semantics_source.notes: This document is the output contract only: file paths, schemas, exact key sets, identifier payloads and checksum encodings. It does NOT define how values are derived.
semantics_source.authority: Normalization, dedupe tie-breaks, interval and overlap semantics, domain ordering, policy resolution, attenuation, the debt ledger, unit and threshold math, scoring, priority rules and queue ordering were settled by the change-advisory board; the authoritative record is /app/rebuild/index_review_log.md. Where an early draft proposal conflicts with a later CAB decision, the later decision wins.

canonical_shard_label_scope._note: Scope declaration only. The alias table, the trim/lowercase rules and every other canonicalization value are defined authoritatively in /app/rebuild/index_review_log.md; this entry fixes only WHERE the resulting label is used.
canonical_shard_label_scope.rule: Shard labels are canonicalized once -- trimmed, lowercased, then folded through the alias table -- and the resulting canonical label is the shard identity used EVERYWHERE downstream. It is not confined to canonical counting.
applies_to: shard window construction and the window's shard key
policy, exception, handoff, blackout and degrade DOMAIN MATCHING
domain compaction, performed on the folded label, BEFORE any overlap milliseconds are computed
queue rows, their thresholds and every checksum derived from the above
canonical_shard_label_scope.consequence: Two raw labels that fold to the same canonical label are the same shard for compaction and overlap purposes: their policy spans compact together as one domain, and the overlap is computed once against the merged spans. Compacting the raw labels separately and only folding afterwards produces different overlap milliseconds and therefore different durations, queue membership and checksums.

governing_entry_index._note: Navigation aid only. It records WHICH review entries carry governing rules for each pipeline stage; it does not restate any rule, value, divisor, threshold or rounding direction, and it does not indicate which of the entries named for a stage is the current one. A stage may name several entries where a later dated entry revises or reverses an earlier one on a specific point, so being listed here does NOT mean an entry is current in every respect, and being absent from here does NOT by itself establish that an entry is superseded. Read every entry named for a stage in /app/rebuild/index_review_log.md and apply the latest dated ruling on each individual point; the review log is authoritative and this index makes no claim about which entries remain in force.
governing_entry_index.rounding_warning: Rounding direction is not uniform across the pipeline and is not inferable from any neighbouring divisor, including between siblings in the same family. Each divisor's direction is fixed by its own entry above; IDX-2250 recorded the map and is revised by IDX-2264, which is the current map of record.
governing_entry_index.non_normative_entries: IDX-2240, IDX-2243, IDX-2249 and IDX-2262 concern dashboards, archive ingest, publication and access recertification. They carry no estimator semantics.
